BIBLY 「킹제임스 성경 정본역(正本譯)」은 어떤 기존 한국어 역본도.en: The BIBLY “King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation (正本譯)” does not use any existing Korean version as its base text; it is an independent translation made afresh by comparing the KJV directly with the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek originals. This document sets out the principles this translation consistently keeps and the grounds for them.

BIBLY 킹제임스 성경 정본역(正本譯)의 번역 원칙 — 공인본문(TR).en: The translation principles of the BIBLY King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation (正本譯): preserving the text on the basis of the Received Text (TR), final comparison with the Hebrew and Greek originals, distinguishing original terms (Hades/hell), rendering the divine name, and preserving key doctrinal terms.

KJV 자신도 시편 83:18(\"whose name alone is <.en: The KJV itself transliterates and reveals the divine name in Psalm 83:18 ("whose name alone is JEHOVAH"), Exodus 6:3, and Isaiah 12:2 and 26:4. This translation applies that tradition of transliteration consistently throughout the Old Testament.

간혹 '음부(陰府)는 불교에서 온 말'이라는 지적이 있으나 이는 성립하지.en: Some object that eumbu (陰府) is a word that came from Buddhism, but this does not hold. Jiok (地獄, “hell”) is likewise a Sino-Korean word that originated in Buddhist scriptures, and cheonguk (天國, “heaven”) is the same kind of word; by that logic, no Bible that uses jiok or cheonguk would be free of the charge. A Sino-Korean word is only a vessel that holds a concept; its meaning is filled in by the text of Scripture. In fact, the Korean Revised Version and the Revised New Korean Version also use the same word eumbu in the New Testament (Matthew 16:18, “the gates of hell”; Revelation 20:14, “death and hell”) — a word the Korean church has used together for over a hundred years. And Revelation 20:14 says that death and hell themselves are cast into the lake of fire. If eumbu were the final hell, then hell would be cast into hell; so distinguishing the two words is exactly the translation the text requires.

구약의 신명 네 글자(יהוה)는 <b>'여호와'</b>로 옮깁니다. 그.en: The four-letter divine name of the Old Testament (יהוה) is rendered “Yeohowa” (Jehovah), for the following reasons.

구원의 진리를 담는 핵심 용어는 새 단어로 바꾸지 않고 표준 그대로 보존.en: Key terms that carry the truth of salvation are not replaced with new words but kept in their standard form: only begotten Son (doksaengja), eternal life, justification · being declared righteous, grace, truth, Son of man (inja), the Comforter, coming, and others. The New Testament word baptizō (βαπτίζω) is rendered chimrye (baptism by immersion), following the original meaning of being immersed in water.

다니엘 9:25 — <b>마시아흐(מָשִׁיחַ)</b>는 '기름부음받.en: Daniel 9:25 — mashiach (מָשִׁיחַ) is rendered “the Anointed One,” bringing out its meaning.

번역 원칙 — 킹제임스 성경 정본역(正本譯) · BIBLY 바이블 인사이.en: Translation Principles — King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation (正本譯) · BIBLY Bible Insight

번역의 최종 근거는 언제나 <b>히브리어·아람어·헬라어 원문</b>입니다.en: The final authority for translation is always the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek originals. We check the original for every key word, and where an English expression narrows or widens the meaning of the original, the original takes priority.

본 「킹제임스 성경 정본역(正本譯)」은 어떤 기존 한국어 역본도 저본이나.en: This “King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation (正本譯)” is an independent translation that has not used any existing Korean version as its base text or reference text. Copyright in the translated text, footnotes and commentary belongs to Bible Insight (BIBLY), and unauthorized reproduction or copying is prohibited. The English text of the KJV (1611) is in the public domain.

본 번역의 영어 기준 본문은 <b>King James Version(16.en: The English base text of this translation is the King James Version (1611), and it preserves one-to-one the verse structure of the Received Text (Textus Receptus) and the Masoretic Text on which the KJV is based. Therefore, verses that some modern versions omit or bracket (e.g. Mark 16:9–20, Acts 8:37, 1 John 5:7) are translated as part of the text. No verses are omitted.

성경 번역 이야기 — 구절별 번역 노트.en: Bible Translation Notes — Notes Verse by Verse

성경 원어는 죽은 자의 세계와 최후 형벌의 장소를 서로 다른 단어로 말합.en: The original languages of the Bible use different words for the world of the dead and for the place of final punishment. This translation preserves that distinction in Korean.

스가랴 12:10 — <b>다카르(דָּקַר)</b>는 '찌른 바'로.en: Zechariah 12:10 — daqar (דָּקַר) is rendered “pierced,” preserving the force of the original.

아울러 음부가 형벌 없는 중립 지대가 아님은 본문이 스스로 증언합니다(누.en: Moreover, the text itself testifies that hell (eumbu) is not a neutral zone without punishment (Luke 16:23 — “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments…”). We believe that rendering the hell of Gehenna as jiok, and the hell of Sheol and Hades as eumbu, is the way that neither adds to nor takes from the original.

이 구분은 KJV 영역 자체의 관행과도 일치합니다. KJV는 스올 65회.en: This distinction also agrees with the practice of the KJV's own English translation. The KJV rendered the 65 occurrences of Sheol, according to context, as hell 31 times · grave 31 times · pit 3 times. In other words, the KJV translators themselves did not uniformly render Sheol with a single word. This translation adds an original-language footnote to every such verse (some 70 places), openly showing within the text which word was rendered and how — you can check it directly in the 📖 footnotes on the Bible reading screen.

종결어미는 소리 내어 읽기에 합당한 <b>권위체</b>(~이라 · ~하시.en: Sentence endings use a dignified style fit for reading aloud (-ira · -hasinira · -neunira · -roda), and place and personal names keep the traditional forms the Korean church has long used (Aegup for Egypt, Damesek for Damascus, Gamnamsan for the Mount of Olives, etc.).

킹제임스 성경 정본역(正本譯) · Translation Principle.en: King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation (正本譯) · Translation Principles

한국 교회 130년의 기도와 찬송이 이 이름 위에 서 있습니다. 익숙한.en: 130 years of the Korean church's prayers and hymns stand on this name. We judged that keeping the familiar name while preserving the distinction in the original is the wisest path.

한국어에서 신명(יהוה)과 주(아도나이, אֲדֹנָי)를 모두 '주'.en: In Korean, if both the divine name (יהוה) and Lord (Adonai, אֲדֹנָי) are rendered “Ju” (Lord), the two titles cannot be told apart. Only by rendering “Yeohowa” and “Ju” separately can double titles such as “Ju Yeohowa” (Adonai Yahweh, “Lord GOD”) be kept just as in the original.
